order_note: After SQL 170 (aws/workflows/sql/170_check_endorsement_email_status.sql, applied to production 2026-11-19): SQL 172 adds what a payee's endorsement request needs to show when Resend reported the request email opened and a link in it clicked, next to Delivered (owner 2026-11-23, "Yes build opened and clicked"). It finds the endorsement by SQL 170's email_message_id, exactly as SQL 170's aws_endorsement_email_event does, and needs that column and function: the file refuses (55000) sql172_prerequisite_missing without them, and the release engine refuses with predecessors_applied unless SQL 170's objects read its pinned intended fingerprint (e53dd2feaae35238f25a194cae9bc4d6356c21d4ad616051180c162eb59b0c81). On public.check_endorsements: six new columns, email_first_opened_at, email_last_opened_at, email_first_clicked_at, email_last_clicked_at (timestamptz, nullable, no default) and email_open_count, email_click_count (integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0); no column grant (the table SELECT for checksops already covers new columns). One new SECURITY DEFINER function (plpgsql, VOLATILE, search_path public, row_security off; EXECUTE checksops and the owner, revoked from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role): aws_endorsement_email_engagement(text, text, timestamp with time zone) returning boolean ('opened' or 'clicked': first time once, latest time the later one, count plus one; any other kind or an unknown or blank id changes nothing and returns false). The file also refuses (55000) sql172_definer_cannot_write (the applying login must own check_endorsements without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or be a superuser or BYPASSRLS; the engine's definer_can_write_relations) and sql172_column_conflict (a new column already present with another type, NOT NULL or default). No SQL 170 object, policy, trigger, index, table grant, other column or row change beyond the two counts' default. Expected pre-state in both environments: everything absent (release sql172 v1: dbf6a7240cfc5dd737cd47e7f0f765cf6349c0a3a8625a39e02f4901c2e29897, releaseStateHash('sql172', {})). The API that passes Resend's email.opened and email.clicked events to the function (with open and click tracking on for the sending domain) and the website that shows them are later, separate changes (a Lambda overlay and a website upload, after this pin is applied in production). No API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.
